verdict.root_cause: productcatalogservice is deliberately failing a subset of GetProduct calls because its "ProductCatalogService Fail" feature flag is enabled. Every frontend error line is the same gRPC status 13 INTERNAL whose detail names ProductCatalogService and attributes the failure to an enabled failure flag, with stack frames entirely in the gRPC client receive-status path [tr_3e27ef5433f4]. Traces localise the origin: the deepest ERROR-marked span in every failing trace is productcatalogservice's own GetProduct handler, while its FeatureFlagService/GetFlag child and the cart, redis and recommendation subtrees complete cleanly [tr_6535606ca4c9]. Failures are sub-millisecond rejections, so no timeout or saturation is involved [tr_6535606ca4c9]. Both services moved from exactly-zero baselines to a late abrupt burst with a single change point at 22:46:30 and ~8-9% peaks [tr_052539fa47ec][tr_10633b596234]. The wrong configuration value is itself the mechanism: the request is rejected because the flag says to reject it.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals converge. Frontend logs name both the failing dependency and the mechanism, and 13 INTERNAL with an application-level detail excludes transport failure, deadline exceeded and frontend-internal defects [tr_3e27ef5433f4]. Traces independently place the error origin at productcatalogservice's GetProduct server span with the flag-lookup child unmarked, excluding the reading that productcatalogservice merely relays a downstream error [tr_6535606ca4c9]. Metrics fix timing and shape: flat-zero baselines, one change point at 22:46:30, partial ~8-9% failure — the signature of selective flag-driven rejection, not exhaustion or an unstartable artifact [tr_052539fa47ec][tr_10633b596234]. Change records argue against competing classes: productcatalogservice has no deploy or image bump, and its only entries are a traffic-shaping injection fully removed ~14.6h before onset [tr_52ddbb1a47d0]; cartservice's chaos actions are all reverted, the last ~1.1h before onset [tr_7ac3e89dc0a4]. Because requests fail fast and by decision, latency and exhaustion are not the mechanism; because the artifact is unchanged, this is not a wrong image. Disabling the flag is what makes the service stop rejecting. Blame sits on productcatalogservice, not frontend: frontend's and checkout's errors both follow from productcatalogservice returning INTERNAL to callers.
open_questions: No change record shows the flag being flipped, by whom or when; the flag state is inferred from error detail text and trace topology, and featureflagservice's change history was never queried.
productcatalogservice's own logs were never read — the Loki selector used a hyphenated label and returned zero lines over four hours including healthy periods [tr_441f94b6fe9a].

Timing and scope are unsettled: frontend errors appear at ~22:45:05 while metric change points are at 22:46:30 with the intervening logs dropped [tr_3e27ef5433f4], and why only ~8-9% of calls and only GetProduct fail is unexplained; 4 of the 7 in-radius services were never measured.

alternatives.root_cause: featureflagservice served a wrong flag value and productcatalogservice is faithfully honouring it.
alternatives.why_not: The GetFlag child span returns in ~1ms with no error marker [tr_6535606ca4c9], so the flag store behaved as designed; the rejecting behaviour lives in productcatalogservice's handler. featureflagservice was never dispatched, so this shifts only ownership, not mechanism or fix.

alternatives.root_cause: Residual chaos-experiment state on cartservice or productcatalogservice (REDIS_ADDR override, traffic shaping) was still degrading the call path at onset.
alternatives.why_not: Every injected condition has a matching revert completing 1.1-14.6h before onset [tr_7ac3e89dc0a4][tr_52ddbb1a47d0], and cart/redis spans complete cleanly inside the failing traces [tr_6535606ca4c9].
